ai.literal: Suitable opportunity if seen, for striking anvil, not agreeing those who associate friendship.
ai.translation: The friendship of those who outwardly associate but inwardly disagree is like an anvil, supporting you only to strike when the right opportunity arises.
ai.modern: மனத்தால் பொருந்தாமல் வெளியளவில் நெருங்கிப் பழகும் பகைவரின் நட்பானது, தக்க சமயம் கிடைக்கும்போது வெட்டுவதற்குத் தாங்கும் பட்டடையைப் போன்றதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against false friends who outwardly act close but inwardly harbor enmity. Their friendship is compared to an anvil used by a blacksmith. Just as the anvil supports the metal only so it can be struck with a hammer, these false friends support you only until they find the right opportunity to strike and ruin you.

ai.literal: Kin resembling, kin those-who-are-not friendship, women mind like different will-become.
ai.translation: The friendship of those who look like your own kind but are not will change, just like the minds of fickle women.
ai.modern: தமக்கு நெருக்கமானவர்களைப் போல நடித்து உண்மையில் அன்பில்லாதவர்களின் நட்பு, நிலையற்ற மனமுடைய மகளிரின் மனம்போல அடிக்கடி மாறிக்கொண்டே இருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against false friends who pretend to be part of one's inner circle. The word 'இனம்' (inam) means one's own kind or kin, representing true, loyal friends. Those who only resemble true friends but are not will not remain loyal. Their friendship is compared to the minds of 'மகளிர்' (makaḷir, women)—which in this specific context implies women whose affections are fickle and transactional. Just as their minds constantly shift, the loyalty of false friends will change when it suits them.

ai.literal: Many good things learned even after, mind-good people becoming, to those lacking excellence is difficult.
ai.translation: Even after learning many good things, it is difficult for those lacking true excellence to become good at heart.
ai.modern: பல நல்ல நூல்களைக் கற்றாலும், மாண்பு இல்லாதவர்கள் மனத்தால் நல்லவர்களாக மாறுவது கடினம்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains that mere education cannot change the fundamental nature of ignoble people. The word 'மாணார்' refers to those who lack true inner excellence or noble character. Even if such people learn many good things, they cannot achieve a good heart. Thus, their friendship remains false and dangerous despite their outward learning.

ai.literal: On the face sweetly smiling, in the mind evil, deceitful people to fear must be.
ai.translation: One must fear deceitful people who smile sweetly on their faces but harbor evil in their hearts.
ai.modern: முகத்தில் இனிமையாகச் சிரித்து, மனத்திற்குள் தீமையை வைத்திருக்கும் வஞ்சகர்களைக் கண்டு அஞ்ச வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against false friends who hide their true intentions. The phrase 'முகத்தின் இனிய நகாஅ' describes their outward behavior, smiling sweetly to appear friendly. However, 'அகத்து இன்னா' reveals their true nature, holding evil or harm in their minds. Because of this dangerous contradiction, such deceitful people must be feared and avoided.

ai.literal: In mind those who do not agree, in whatever measure anything, by word, of the nature of trusting it is not.
ai.translation: It is never right to trust the words of those whose minds do not agree with yours, no matter what they say.
ai.modern: மனத்தால் நம்மோடு பொருந்தாதவர்களை, அவர்கள் சொல்லும் சொற்களைக் கொண்டு எந்த அளவிலும் நம்புவது கூடாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against trusting people who harbor inner enmity while speaking friendly words. The phrase 'மனத்தின் அமையாதவரை' refers to those whose minds are not aligned or in harmony with ours. 'எனைத்தொன்றும்' emphasizes that one should not trust them even a little bit or in any matter. 'சொல்லினால் தேறற்பாற்று அன்று' concludes that relying merely on their spoken words is not a trustworthy course of action, as their outward speech contradicts their inner feelings.

ai.literal: Like friends, good things even if they say, foes' words quickly will be perceived.
ai.translation: Even if foes speak pleasant words as though they were friends, the true nature of their words will quickly be understood.
ai.modern: நண்பர்களைப் போல நல்ல வார்த்தைகளைச் சொன்னாலும், பகைவர்களின் சொற்களின் உண்மைத் தன்மை விரைவாகப் புரிந்து கொள்ளப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns about the deceptive speech of enemies who pretend to be well-wishers. The word 'நட்டார்' refers to true friends who have formed a genuine bond, while 'ஒட்டார்' refers to foes who do not truly unite or agree with you. Even if these enemies speak pleasant and agreeable words ('நல்லவை'), their underlying hostility cannot be hidden for long. The phrase 'ஒல்லை உணரப்படும்' emphasizes that the deceitful nature of their words will swiftly be perceived by a discerning mind.

ai.literal: Word humility foes-with do-not-accept bow bending harm because-of-intending.
ai.translation: Do not accept the humble words of foes, for the bending of a bow intends only harm.
ai.modern: பகைவர்கள் பணிவாகப் பேசும் சொற்களை நம்பி ஏற்றுக்கொள்ளக் கூடாது. ஏனென்றால், வில் வளைவது ஒருவருக்குத் தீங்கு செய்வதையே நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டது.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against trusting the submissive or polite speech of enemies. The word 'வணக்கம்' is used brilliantly in two senses: the humility of words and the physical bending of a bow. Just as a bow bends only to shoot an arrow and cause harm, an enemy's humble words are a deceptive posture meant to strike when the time is right. Therefore, one should never accept such false humility.

ai.translation: Even within the folded hands of foes, a weapon may lie hidden. The tears they weep are of the exact same nature.
ai.modern: பகைவர்கள் வணங்கிக் கைகூப்பும் போது அந்தக் கைகளுக்கு உள்ளேயும் ஆயுதம் மறைந்திருக்கலாம். அவர்கள் அழுது வடிக்கின்ற கண்ணீரும் அத்தகையதே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against trusting the outward displays of emotion or respect from deceitful enemies. Just as a deadly weapon can be concealed within hands folded in respectful greeting, the tears shed by foes are equally deceptive and dangerous. The word 'aṉaittu' (of that nature) connects the hidden weapon to the tears, showing both are mere covers for hidden malice.

ai.literal: abundantly having done, oneself those who despise, to smile having made, within friendship to die embracing is the nature.
ai.translation: When dealing with those who show exaggerated affection but secretly despise you, it is wise to make them smile outwardly while letting the friendship die in your embrace.
ai.modern: வெளியில் மிகவும் அன்பாக நடந்துகொண்டு உள்ளத்தில் தம்மை இகழ்பவர்களை, வெளியிலும் சிரித்து மகிழும்படி செய்து, ஆனால் அகத்தில் அந்த நட்பு சாகும்படி பழகுவதே அறிவுடையோர் இயல்பாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises on how to handle false friends who show exaggerated affection outwardly but mock you inwardly. Instead of confronting them, one should match their outward behavior by making them smile and acting friendly. However, internally, one should let the friendship wither and die, maintaining only a superficial embrace. The word 'சா' (to die) powerfully contrasts with 'புல்லல்' (embracing), showing that the relationship should be allowed to perish even while maintaining outward pleasantries.

ai.explanation: This couplet advises caution when enemies suddenly pretend to be friends. The phrase 'பகைநட்பாம் காலம்' refers to a time when foes act friendly for their own benefit. In such situations, one should respond with 'முகநட்டு' (outward or facial friendship) to be polite and safe. However, one must completely abandon 'அகநட்பு' (inner or true friendship) to protect oneself from their hidden deceit.
